## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Color spaces
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Color spaces and color science
//  - Device-independent color models
//  - Palettes, harmony, and color difference
//  - Device-referred and video color models

//==
// # Color spaces and color science
//
// The vocabulary that *defines* a color space: chromaticity coordinates, white
// points and standard illuminants, primaries, transfer characteristics, and the
// chromatic adaptation and rendering intent a conversion between two spaces
// needs. The color representations themselves are the device-independent and
// device-referred/video sections below.
// Conversions are functions in a later pass; these types name the endpoints
// and the knobs.

//==
// ## Chromaticity and white points

// A CIE 1931 xy chromaticity coordinate: a color's hue-and-purity position on
// the chromaticity diagram, independent of luminance.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromaticity)
type Chromaticity
    implements IValue, IHashable
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
}

// A reference white: the chromaticity the color space treats as achromatic,
// with its luminance in candelas per square meter (0 when unspecified).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_point)
type WhitePoint
    implements IValue
{
    Chromaticity: Chromaticity;
    Luminance: Number;
}

// A standard CIE illuminant used as a reference white. A is incandescent;
// E is equal energy. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_illuminant)
type StandardIlluminant
    = A | B | C | D50 | D55 | D60 | D65 | D75 | E | F2 | F7 | F11;

//==
// ## Primaries, transfer functions, and RGB color spaces

// An opto-electronic transfer characteristic: how linear light is encoded to
// (and decoded from) stored component values. SRGB is the piecewise sRGB
// curve; Rec709 is the BT.1886 pair; PQ (SMPTE ST 2084) and HLG (hybrid
// log-gamma) are the HDR encodings.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_functions_in_imaging)
type TransferFunction
    = Linear | SRGB | Gamma18 | Gamma22 | Gamma24 | Gamma26 | Rec709 | PQ | HLG;

// The chromaticities of an RGB color space's three primaries and its white
// point; together they fix the space's gamut and its matrix to CIE XYZ.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_color)
type RgbPrimaries
    implements IValue
{
    Red: Chromaticity;
    Green: Chromaticity;
    Blue: Chromaticity;
    White: Chromaticity;
}

// A fully specified RGB color space: named primaries plus a transfer
// characteristic. Sufficient to convert between the space and CIE XYZ.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RGB_color_spaces)
type RgbColorSpace
    implements IValue
{
    Name: String;
    Primaries: RgbPrimaries;
    Transfer: TransferFunction;
}

// A well-known RGB color space, for when a name is enough and the full
// RgbColorSpace record is not needed.
type NamedColorSpace
    = SRGB
    | LinearSRGB
    | DisplayP3
    | AdobeRGB
    | ProPhotoRGB
    | Rec709
    | Rec2020
    | ACEScg
    | ACES2065;

// The strategy for mapping colors between the gamuts of two color spaces
// (the ICC rendering intents). (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_management)
type RenderingIntent
    = Perceptual | RelativeColorimetric | Saturation | AbsoluteColorimetric;

// A method for adapting tristimulus values from one white point to another.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatic_adaptation)
type ChromaticAdaptation = XyzScaling | Bradford | VonKries | CAT02 | CAT16;

// A conversion recipe between two named color spaces, including the chromatic
// adaptation to use when their white points differ.
type ColorSpaceConversion
    implements IValue
{
    Source: NamedColorSpace;
    Target: NamedColorSpace;
    Adaptation: ChromaticAdaptation;
    Intent: RenderingIntent;
}

//==
// # Device-independent color models
//
// Colors expressed in spaces that do not depend on any particular device: the
// CIE tristimulus hub (`ColorXYZ`) that conversions pass through, its xyY
// factoring, and the perceptual (uniform-ish) spaces built on top of it —
// CIELAB, CIELUV, and OkLab, each with a cylindrical lightness/chroma/hue
// form. The spaces themselves are defined in `color-spaces`.

//==
// ## Device-independent color types

// A color as CIE 1931 XYZ tristimulus values; the device-independent hub
// through which color space conversions pass. Y is luminance.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIE_1931_color_space)
type ColorXYZ
    implements INumerical
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
    Z: Number;
}

// A color as an xy chromaticity plus luminance Y (the CIE xyY form);
// separates "which color" from "how bright".
type ColorXyY
    implements IValue
{
    Chromaticity: Chromaticity;
    Luminance: Number;
}

// A color in CIELAB: perceptual lightness L in [0, 100] with opponent axes
// A (green-red) and B (blue-yellow), relative to a reference white.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIELAB_color_space)
type ColorLab
    implements IValue
{
    L: Number;
    A: Number;
    B: Number;
}
```
